Our Solutions Architects and Forward Deployed Engineers are aligned to accounts, segments and Account Executives. This role isn't. As a Principal Field Engineer, you work across the whole business: every region, every segment, presales and post-sales. Your job is to make Exa impossible to ignore for developers and technical buyers, and to make every Field Engineer better at showing what Exa can do.

You'll build the demos, workshops and on-demand training the team and our customers use everywhere, take Exa on the road to conferences, meetups and user groups, and become the go-to expert the team pulls in when a deal or a customer needs someone who knows Exa inside out. You'll spend a lot of time where developers are, and a lot of time on a plane. This is not a slideware role. You are an engineer who builds, teaches and shows.

In this role, you will:

  • Build the demos the whole team uses: flagship demos, sample apps, cookbooks and reference architectures that show Exa on real problems, and keep them current as the product ships

  • Design and deliver workshops, hands-on labs and technical webinars for prospects, customers and developer communities, and package them so any Field Engineer can run them

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role

You design the mechanics of our robotic hands — from the kinematics of a single finger to a complete hand ready for series production.

Multiple drives, gear trains, tendons, tactile sensors and electronics have to fit into a human-sized envelope while surviving hundreds of thousands of cycles. Every millimetre matters, and almost every design decision affects another discipline.

You work hands-on between CAD, test rig and workshop, and report to the CTO.

What you will do:

  • CAD design. Design components, mechanisms and assemblies within tightly constrained envelopes, owning the design from concept through production release.

  • Mechanism & kinematics. Design finger and thumb kinematics, tendon and spindle drives, joints and bearings. Calculate motion envelopes, trajectories, gripping forces and transmission ratios.

  • Calculation & validation. Validate designs through structural and fatigue calculations, FEA, tolerance stack-ups and GD&T before parts are manufactured.

  • Material selection. Select and qualify materials for lightweight structures, wear surfaces, tendons and elastomeric gripping surfaces, and characterise their behaviour under real loads and contact conditions.

  • Assembly design. Design assemblies for efficient assembly, adjustment-free interfaces, serviceability and repair. Specify the required fixtures and tooling.

  • Design for manufacturing. Design for the intended manufacturing process from the outset — machining, injection moulding, sheet metal, additive manufacturing — balancing cost, tolerances and production volumes.

  • Prototyping & testing. Build prototypes, design test rigs and endurance setups, run cycle and load tests, and drive failures to root cause.

  • Documentation & release. Create drawings and BOMs, manage design changes and configuration, and support product development reviews.

  • Suppliers & production. Work with machine shops, material suppliers and manufacturing partners from first prototype through pilot series and production ramp-up.

  • Cross-functional integration. Work closely with Electronics, Sensors and Software to align packaging, interfaces and load paths across the complete system.

What you bring:

  • Degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, precision engineering, or a comparable qualification.

  • 5–10 years of experience in mechanical design of precision mechatronic products, including at least one product taken through to series production.

  • Advanced 3D CAD skills in CATIA, NX, SolidWorks, Creo or comparable systems, with confident 2D drawing creation and GD&T.

  • Strong understanding of mechanism design: linkages, gear trains, bearings, shafts, power transmission, backlash and stiffness.

  • Experience with FEA, structural and fatigue analysis, and tolerance calculations as part of everyday design work.

  • Strong knowledge of material selection for lightweight, high-load and wear-critical components.

  • Practical DFM/DFA experience across multiple manufacturing processes.

  • Hands-on mentality — you build the prototype, run the test and analyse the broken part yourself.

  • Fluent in English and German.

Bonus:

  • Experience with robotic hands, grippers, prosthetics or similarly highly integrated mechanisms.

  • Experience with compact drive trains, including planetary, harmonic or cycloidal gearing, spindle drives and actuator integration.

  • Experience with elastomers, soft goods, injection moulding of complex geometries or compliant structures.

  • Experience integrating tactile or force sensors into mechanical structures.

  • Experience with multi-body simulation or topology optimisation.

  • Knowledge of Machinery Regulation, ISO/TS 15066 and mechanical design for collaborative applications.

The next chapter of robotics won't be built in a lab. It will be built by people who care about what happens when technology meets the real world.

At TACTILIA, you'll work on one of the hardest open problems in robotics: giving machines the dexterity, reliability and robustness to interact with the physical world at industrial scale.

The technology is taking shape, the team is being built, and the standards around robotic hands and their skills are still open. That means your decisions will have a lasting impact — not just on a product, but on what comes next for Physical AI.

Build the hand. Define the standard. Shape what comes next.

If you're excited by the challenge of building robotic hands that works reliably in the real world, we'd love to hear from you.

That system is your product. You build what AI generates against: the design system and component architecture, the generation and agent workflows, the quality gates that keep output production-ready, and the feedback loops that keep it all visible to the team. You stay hands-on as a designer, because the quickest way to prove the system works is to ship real interfaces on top of it.

This is a senior individual contributor role in Product Design. You split your time between Figma and a code editor in roughly equal measure. You work directly with design leadership to drive AI adoption across the whole design organisation, and you sit in a cross-functional team with Engineering and Product.

What you are expected to do:

Build the system

  • Architect the design system, tokens and components as the substrate AI generates against.

  • Design prompt libraries, patterns and agent workflows that turn design intent into production-ready UI with minimal human assembly.

Prove it by designing

  • Stay a practising designer. Explore concepts quickly and design real interfaces.

  • Prototype in production front-end code. You are the first and toughest test of whether the system produces excellent, shippable work.

Own quality, guardrails and evals

  • Define production-readiness criteria for AI-generated UI.

  • Set design-to-code fidelity benchmarks, regression safeguards and evaluation methods that keep AI output honest. Speed must not cost craft.

Drive the AI workflow across the design org

  • Work with design leadership to maintain, evolve and roll out the AI-native workflow across the whole design organisation, not only your own work.

  • Collaborate closely with Engineering, Product and design-system contributors. You complement engineering and do not replace it.

  • Keep the system round-tripping to shared surfaces such as Figma. AI-accelerated output stays visible and open to feedback, never a black box.

Push into generative UI

  • Take AI beyond the build process and into the product itself.

  • Turn what works into playbooks, prompt libraries and enablement. The wider design org builds on the system and does not depend on you. The goal is durable capability, not tool dependency.

title: Deployment Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
🎤 Why voize? Because we’re more than just a job!

At voize, we believe the greatest gift to frontline workers is time - time to care, connect, and be present. Today, that time is lost to busywork and complex systems that pull them away from what matters most: people.

Our vision is to change that by building AI companions that seamlessly take over digital workflows. We don't replace humans with technology - we amplify their impact.

Our mission is backed with a $50M Series A funding led by Balderton Capital, with support from HV Capital, Y Combinator and other leading VCs. Today, 2,000+ facilities trust voize, and over 200,000 users rely on our AI companion to ease their daily workload.

As a dynamic team, we combine first-in-class technology with meaningful social impact. And now, we’re looking for you to join us on this mission!

💡 Your Mission: Delight customers, optimise processes!

As a Deployment Engineer at voize, you own the full technical journey of our customers - from the first presales check to ongoing operations. You’re the primary technical point of contact, bridging voize and customer IT. By validating infrastructure, configuring secure setups, solving technical issues, and scaling deployments, you ensure a smooth experience and long-term success.

🚀 Your Daily Business – No two days are alike

  • Support pre-sales calls to assess infrastructure, spot blockers, and guide evaluations

  • Several years of experience as a Linux or Windows Administrator

  • Troubleshoot issues across systems, networks, browsers, and interfaces with clarity and empathy

  • Support technical scaling (e.g. growing user bases, infra changes)

  • Document setups and technical handoffs for smooth internal collaboration

  • Flag recurring issues and contribute to internal tools, docs, or processes

🤝 Your Skillset – What you bring to the table

  • Expert Windows/Linux system administration and network configuration skills (firewalls, proxies, routing, MDMs, APIs)

  • Solid experience with virtualisation, Docker, web servers (Nginx, IIS), and load balancing

  • Excellent troubleshooting skills across APIs, browsers, infrastructure, and devices

  • Clear communicator with empathy for both technical and non-technical users

  • Proactive, self-directed, and skilled in documentation and technical handoffs

  • Experience with start-ups will help you thrive in this role

  • You’re confident in German (C2) to support customers and fluent in English (C1) to work closely with colleagues - we’ll support you with language courses if needed.

🌱 Growing together – what you can expect at voize

  • We are a fast-growing startup, that means you will tackle challenges, grow quickly, and make a real impact, giving healthcare professionals more time for real patient care

  • We foster an open, collaborative culture with regular team events, whether you work from our Berlin office or remotely from Germany

  • Become a co-creator of our success with stock options

  • Generous perks: 30 vacation days plus your birthday off, Germany Transport Ticket, Urban Sports Club, regular company off-sites, and access to learning platforms such as Blinkist and Audible

  • You decide when you work best, that means flexible working hours and a good hybrid set-up.

✨ Ready to talk? Apply now! 🚀

We look forward to your application and can’t wait to meet you – no matter who you are or what background you have!

title: Senior ML Engineer - NLP (m/f/d)
description:
🎤 Why voize?

At voize, we believe the greatest gift to frontline workers is time: time to care, connect and be present. Our AI helps care professionals turn spoken notes into structured documentation, so they can spend less time on administrative work and more time with people.

More than 200,000 care workers use voize. Join us to build technology that makes a difference in their daily work.

💡 Your mission

Build agents that nurses can trust: accurate, fast and safe enough for real-world care. You’ll combine hands-on ML with thoughtful engineering and rigorous evaluation, using production data and feedback to improve the product.

We’re hiring four ML engineers through one process. Depending on your strengths and interests, you’ll work on hospital documentation, US senior care, German care agents or the shared NLP platform. You’ll be part of the NLP chapter and work closely with product and engineering colleagues.

🚀 What you’ll do

  • Build and improve LLM agent workflows for nursing forms, assessments, care reports and care-plan suggestions, working on tools, context, state and prompts.

  • Own evaluation for your area: create benchmarks from production traces and synthetic scenarios, build regression tests and use results to inform what ships.

  • Investigate real-world failures, reproduce issues across the app, backend and models, and turn what you learn into fixes, tests and data-labeling tasks.

  • Train or adapt models where they outperform rented frontier models on quality, speed, cost or privacy—for example, for personal-data detection or smaller, faster models.

  • Make latency, cost and privacy part of your engineering decisions, from model routing and caching to protecting sensitive data.

  • Partner with product, engineering, data and customer-facing teams, and use feedback from care professionals to guide improvements.

🤝 What you bring

  • Experience training, evaluating and shipping ML or NLP models to production, and explaining the decisions and results behind your work.

  • Experience building evaluations for ML or LLM systems and using error analysis and regression tests to guide product decisions.

  • Hands-on experience with LLMs in production, including agents or tool use, structured outputs and context design.

  • Strong software engineering skills: you write tested, reviewable production code and can learn an unfamiliar language or framework.

  • An end-to-end approach to messy problems, sound judgment with sensitive data, and the ownership to work through ambiguity in a fast-paced product team.

  • Fluent English.

🛠️ Our stack

Our ML and evaluation tooling uses Python; our agent and app code uses Kotlin Multiplatform and JetBrains Koog. We use Claude through our inference service, alongside open and on-device models where they make sense. You don’t need to know our specific languages or frameworks before joining: depth and the ability to learn matter more than a keyword match.

🌱 What you can expect

  • Work on a product used by care professionals, with direct feedback and a clear social impact.

  • Shape a young agent stack and grow into ownership of a domain, market or technical area.

  • Do real ML work, from training and evaluation to production, alongside collaborative engineering and product teams.

  • Join a team that values written communication, shared learning and regular time together.

  • Become a co-creator of our success with stock options and access to language courses.

✨ Ready to talk?

Apply to join us in giving care professionals more time for people. We look forward to hearing about the systems you’ve built, what you learned and the impact they had.
